outcome: Since 26 January 2024 one preprint bears on the sphere question: Wang, Wang and Zhou (arXiv 2602.03984, posted 3 Feb 2026, v2 11 Aug 2026) construct an embedded non-equatorial minimal hypersphere in the unit 4-sphere by equivariant min-max. That case was already covered negatively by Hsiang (1983) and, for embedded hyperspheres, by Carlotto and Schulz (2021); the preprint is unrefereed; and I found nothing that moves the open range Wikipedia lists (odd ambient dimensions of 9 or more in its second formulation).
problem_asks: The statement names one problem, 'the spherical Bernstein's problem', and calls it a generalization of Bernstein's problem. It does not spell the question out, so the parts below are taken from the problem's standard form as Wikipedia's January 2024 article gives it, not from later results. (1) Primary reading, Chern's question (1969; ICM Nice 1970): for each n, are the equators of S^(n+1) the only smooth embedded minimal hypersurfaces that are topological n-spheres? This is one question over all dimensions n. (2) The second formulation Wikipedia gives: for each n, is every embedded minimal (n-1)-sphere in S^n totally geodesic, that is an equator? This is the same question with the dimension shifted by one. (3) The third formulation Wikipedia gives: for n = 3, the affirmative answer is equivalent to saying the local topology at an isolated singular point of a minimal hypersurface in an arbitrary Riemannian 4-manifold cannot be that of a disc. (4) Chern's higher-codimension form, which the 2026 literature paraphrases: compact minimal (n-1)-submanifolds of S^n are totally geodesic when their normal planes do not turn too much (the Gauss-image variants of Jost, Xin and Yang fall here). (5) Wikipedia also notes the problem can be generalized by replacing S^(n+1) with a simply connected compact symmetric space (Hsiang, Hsiang and Tomter). I have treated (1) as the bullet's question and (2) and (3) as restatements of it. (4) and (5) are variants; I have recorded results on them as discounted events. The Euclidean entire-graph analogue is not asked by this bullet and was not researched beyond the search results.

events.what_happened: Tongrui Wang, Zhichao Wang and Xin Zhou, 'Equivariant min-max theory and the spherical Bernstein problem in S^4', arXiv:2602.03984 (math.DG). Abstract: 'We construct an embedded non-equatorial minimal hypersphere in the unit 4-sphere S^4, which provides a new resolution of Chern's spherical Bernstein problem in S^4', built from equivariant min-max theory for G-invariant minimal hypersurfaces with reduced genus bound, where G is a compact Lie group acting with 3-dimensional orbit space; the authors say it confirms an assertion made by Pitts-Rubinstein in 1986. Theorem 1.2 (v2 HTML) gives an embedded non-equatorial minimal S^3, an embedded minimal T^3 and an embedded minimal S^1 x S^2 in S^4, all invariant under an S^1 action (suspension of the Hopf action). The introduction lists n = 4 among Hsiang's 1983 dimensions for non-equatorial minimal hyperspheres, n in {4,5,6,7,8,10,12,14}, and says Tomter extended the examples to all even n = 2m >= 4. The abstract page gives 78 pages and 6 figures.
events.revisions: v1 3 Feb 2026; v2 11 Aug 2026 (the current version per the arXiv abstract page). The v2 comment says it adds an embedded minimal S^1 x S^2 in S^4, which the v2 HTML includes as part of Theorem 1.2. No other v2 change was identified. A search snippet listed only v1 and '74 pages'; the abstract page I opened shows v2.
events.delivers: Within problem_asks: in ambient S^4 (hypersphere S^3 in S^4, first formulation n = 3), an embedded minimal S^3 that is not an equator. Existence only, by min-max, with the S^1 symmetry stated in Theorem 1.2. Restricted to S^4; no other dimension. The T^3 and S^1 x S^2 in S^4 are not hyperspheres, so they are not objects of Chern's question. The paper itself records that Hsiang already produced non-equatorial hyperspheres in S^4.
events.remains: Chern's question (1) and its restatement (2) in every dimension other than ambient S^4, including the odd ambient dimensions of 9 or more that Wikipedia lists as unknown. Formulation (3) is not addressed as far as I read. In S^4, the existence question was already answered negatively by Hsiang (1983) and by Carlotto and Schulz (2021) before this preprint.
events.time_since_posted: about 8 months (3 Feb to 13 Oct 2026). No journal acceptance, referee report, published comment, expert write-up or blog post was found in 37 searches. The only later reference I found is by the first author in a June 2026 preprint (see later_work_cites_it), which is self-citation, not verification.
events.doubts: No specific error has been identified. Points for the judging pass: (a) it is an unrefereed preprint; (b) it calls its S^4 case a 'new resolution', yet its own introduction lists n = 4 among Hsiang's 1983 hyperspheres, and Carlotto and Schulz's 2021 abstract reports infinitely many minimally embedded hyperspheres in S^4 (see the priority dispute); the abstract does not say in what sense the result is new; (c) the year of the Pitts-Rubinstein assertion it confirms is given as 1986 here and 1988 elsewhere (see disputes). Reading limits: the fetch returned the abstract, the introduction, Theorem 1.2 and part of Section 4 of the v2 HTML; the final section, the full acknowledgements and the references were not returned. Anything there is unread.
events.direction: Against the expected answer that the equators are the only embedded minimal hyperspheres: it exhibits a non-equatorial one in S^4. This cuts against the conjecture in dimension four only.
events.object: An embedded minimal hypersphere S^3 in the unit S^4 that is not an equator (Theorem 1.2). It is invariant under an S^1 action obtained from a suspended, weighted Hopf action. It is produced as a min-max limit: existence only, with no explicit formula given. Theorem 1.2 also gives an embedded minimal T^3 and an embedded minimal S^1 x S^2 in the same S^4.

events.what_happened: Tongrui Wang, 'Embedded minimal S^1-bundles in S^4', arXiv:2606.31091 (math.DG). Abstract (via the abstract page and a search summary): constructs infinitely many embedded minimal hypersurfaces of pairwise distinct irreducible topological types in S^4, as a new answer to Hsiang's problem on topological types other than S^3, S^1 x S^2, T^3 and SO(3)/(Z2 x Z2). The examples are principal S^1-bundles and Seifert fibered manifolds over closed orientable surfaces; S^1 x Sigma embeds minimally in S^4 for odd genus. Remark 1.3 of the v1 HTML says each Gamma_n 'is topologically either a 3-sphere or an S^1-bundle over an aspherical 2-manifold'. The introduction says the approach is inspired by the equivariant min-max method used in Wang, Wang and Zhou for Chern's problem in S^4.
events.revisions: v1 30 Jun 2026; v2 11 Aug 2026 ('A few details added and some typos corrected', per the comment on the abstract page).
events.delivers: For Chern's question, only what Remark 1.3 implies: some members of the families may be topological 3-spheres. The abstract does not say whether any such member is non-equatorial, and I could not confirm it from the visible text. For the topological-type question actually posed, it gives infinitely many non-sphere types in S^4. That is a different question, Hsiang's topological-type problem.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks, except possibly the S^3 members, which I could not check. Whether those are non-equatorial and embedded is not established by what I read.
events.time_since_posted: about 3.5 months (30 Jun to 13 Oct 2026); no public engagement found.
events.doubts: None specific. Reading limits: the first 100,000 characters of roughly 166,000 were returned; Section 5 (Seifert fibered manifolds) was not visible beyond its table-of-contents entry and the cited theorems 5.3 to 5.5. The proof's Lemma 4.6 is cut off in the visible text.
events.direction: Does not cut directly against the bullet's claim as far as I can read. Its main objects are non-sphere topological types. Its S^3 members, if any, would be non-equatorial examples only if the paper says so, which I could not confirm.
events.object: Infinitely many embedded minimal hypersurfaces in S^4 of pairwise distinct irreducible topological types, principal S^1-bundles over closed orientable surfaces (Gamma_n/S^1) and Seifert fibered manifolds, from equivariant min-max with a suspended, weighted Hopf action. Existence only; no explicit formula.

events.what_happened: Alessandro Carlotto, Yangyang Li and Zhihan Wang, 'Non-persistence of strongly isolated singularities, and geometric applications', arXiv:2411.12677 (math.DG, math.AP). Proves a generic regularity result for stationary varifolds whose singularities are all strongly isolated. Applied to nearly round S^4, it answers in the negative whether the Clifford football and Hsiang's embedded minimal hyperspheres persist under generic nearly round metrics. The paper treats Hsiang's embedded hyperspheres in the round S^4 as known objects. Li gave talks on it at Northwestern (3 Feb 2025) and USTC (16 Dec 2025), per search listings only.
events.delivers: Concerns persistence of the round-S^4 examples under nearly round perturbations. It establishes no new round-sphere example and no new non-equatorial hypersphere. In problem_asks terms it settles nothing, but it corroborates that Hsiang's S^4 hyperspheres are embedded.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, unchanged.
events.time_since_posted: about 23 months. Authorship by experts is not third-party checking; no independent engagement found.
events.direction: Not on the bullet's question. It treats the round-S^4 examples as already obtained, consistent with the negative answer in S^4.

events.what_happened: Nikolaos Kapouleas and Jiahua Zou, 'Minimal hypersurfaces in S^4(1) by doubling the equatorial S^3', arXiv:2405.18283 (math.DG). For each large m, a closed embedded minimal hypersurface in S^4 that doubles the equatorial S^3, with m^2 catenoid-like bridges on an m x m lattice in a Clifford torus; as m tends to infinity it converges to twice the equator. The authors say it answers a question of Yau for S^4 and questions of Hsiang.
events.revisions: v1 28 May 2024; v2 10 Aug 2024 ('an expanded version with further results on the volume and self-shrinkers').
events.delivers: A closed embedded minimal hypersurface in S^4 close to a doubled equator. Its topology is not stated in the abstract. It answers Yau's and Hsiang's questions, not Chern's question about topological spheres.
events.remains: All of problem_asks.
events.time_since_posted: about 17 months; no third-party engagement found.
events.direction: Not against the bullet's question as far as the abstract shows; the object is a doubled equator, not a topological 3-sphere (topology not confirmed).
events.object: A closed embedded minimal hypersurface M_m in S^4 with m^2 catenoid-like bridges, for each large m. Constructed by PDE gluing, so existence only.

events.what_happened: Dongyeong Ko, 'Regularity of cohomogeneity two equivariant isotopy minimization problems and minimal hypersurfaces with large first Betti number on spheres', arXiv:2512.12322 (math.DG). Builds an equivariant min-max theory for cohomogeneity two, described as 'a framework proposed by Pitts and Rubinstein in 1988', and constructs minimal hypersurfaces in round S^(n+1) for 4 <= n+1 <= 7 with SO(n-1) x D_(g+1) symmetry. In dimensions 5 and 6 their topological type is #^(2g)(S^1 x S^(n-1)); for large g they converge to an equator plus a Clifford hypersurface. The abstract does not mention Chern or Hsiang.
events.delivers: No topological sphere is constructed, per the abstract. The examples are non-sphere hypersurfaces, so this does not bear on the bullet's question. It is the source of the 1988 date for the Pitts-Rubinstein proposal (see disputes).

events.what_happened: F. J. Almgren Jr. (Annals of Mathematics, 1966) and E. Calabi (Journal of Differential Geometry, 1967). The lowest case of Chern's question is affirmative: a minimal (immersed) 2-sphere in S^3 is totally geodesic, an equator. Wikipedia's further-reading list and the 2026 WWZ introduction both cite this. I did not open the original papers; the citation is from Wikipedia and the WWZ introduction.
events.delivers: The lowest case only: the 2-sphere in S^3 (second formulation n = 3), under the immersed hypothesis (per WWZ). Affirmative, so equators are the only such objects. It does not reach any higher dimension.
events.remains: Chern's question in every dimension above the lowest case.

events.what_happened: Wu-Yi Hsiang, 'Minimal cones and the spherical Bernstein problem. I', Annals of Mathematics 118 (1983), 61-73. Page range from a citation in search results; the journal page was not opened. Equivariant construction of infinitely many non-congruent minimal hyperspheres in round spheres, using an ODE reduction to geodesics in an orbit space. Per a search summary of Carlotto and Schulz's introduction (not opened), it disproved Chern's conjecture for spheres of dimension 4 and 6. Per Carlotto, Li and Wang (2024), Hsiang's embedded hyperspheres in the round S^4 desingularize the Clifford football.

Wikipedia credits Hsiang with ambient dimensions {4,5,6,7,8,10,12,14} across the 1983 papers and the 1982 note. Which of those this Part I covers was not verified.

Tomter (1987) covers the even ambient dimensions of the second formulation, so the odd range is the one left open.

Existence comes from a dynamical-systems analysis of oscillatory geodesics in the orbit space (per the WWZ introduction's description of the Hsiang-Tomter method). In S^4 they desingularize the Clifford football, the spherical suspension of a Clifford torus. Existence only, with no explicit formula.

Our analysis also yields infinitely many, pairwise non-isometric, minimally embedded hyperspheres and thus provides a self-contained solution to Chern's spherical Bernstein conjecture in dimensions four and six.' Published in Ars Inveniendi Analytica 2023, paper 8.

Regularity for weakly harmonic maps into a sphere whose image avoids a neighbourhood of a half-equator, applied to the spherical and Euclidean Bernstein problems: compact minimal hypersurfaces in spheres are trivial under the new conditions.

events.what_happened: J. Jost, Y. L. Xin and Ling Yang, 'A spherical Bernstein theorem for minimal submanifolds of higher codimension', arXiv:1405.5952, posted 23 May 2014, single version. Spherical and Euclidean Bernstein-type theorems for minimal submanifolds of any dimension and codimension, provided the Gauss image lies in a geometrically defined closed region of a Grassmannian. Proof by a subharmonic auxiliary function, Codazzi equations and geometric measure theory.
events.delivers: A rigidity result for higher codimension under a Gauss-image hypothesis. It is a variant condition, and it does not decide the unconditional question for hyperspheres.
events.remains: The unconditional question, and the hyperspheres of Hsiang and of Carlotto-Schulz, which are not covered by this rigidity statement under the stated hypothesis (not checked).

A compact minimal hypersurface M^k of S^(k+1) with H^1(M) = 0 whose Gauss map omits a neighbourhood of an S^(k-1) equator is totally geodesic. A new proof strategy also gives an analogous result for codimension 2 compact minimal submanifolds; the codimension-2 hypothesis was not visible.

events.direction: Rigidity under extra hypotheses (Gauss-image condition, H^1 = 0), which the codimension-1 abstract states; not an existence result.

disputes.summary: Novelty of the S^4 result. Wang, Wang and Zhou's abstract calls their embedded non-equatorial S^3 in S^4 'a new resolution of Chern's spherical Bernstein problem in S^4'. Their introduction lists n = 4 among Hsiang's 1983 non-equatorial hyperspheres. Carlotto and Schulz's 2021 abstract reports infinitely many minimally embedded hyperspheres in S^4. Carlotto, Li and Wang (2024) treat Hsiang's embedded hyperspheres in round S^4 as known. What, if anything, the 2026 paper adds (for example embeddedness, or a different symmetry class) is not settled by what I could read.

Year of the Pitts-Rubinstein assertion. Wang, Wang and Zhou's abstract says their result confirms 'an assertion made by Pitts-Rubinstein in 1986'. Ko's abstract (Dec 2025) describes the equivariant min-max framework as 'proposed by Pitts and Rubinstein in 1988', and a search summary of Ketover's citation also gives 1988. These may be two different statements or a citation error. Not resolved.

Range of Tomter's result. Wikipedia (January 2024 text, as opened) credits Tomter with all even n in the second formulation and calls odd n >= 9 unknown. The WWZ introduction (opened) says Tomter extended the examples 'to all even dimensions n = 2m >= 4'. A search summary of Chen's 2026 survey (not verified on the abstract page) says Tomter proved a negative answer for every n >= 4. An Encyclopedia of Mathematics snippet (page refused fetch, HTTP 502) gives odd n. Wikipedia's wording that Hsiang and Tomter 'proved it' for listed dimensions reads ambiguously, and the other sources use 'proved' to mean that counterexamples exist.

Dimension indexing. Wikipedia gives two formulations whose dimensions differ by one: a hypersphere in S^(n+1) (first) and an (n-1)-sphere in S^n (second). The dimension lists differ accordingly (Hsiang: {3,4,5,6,7,9,11,13} first, {4,5,6,7,8,10,12,14} second). Secondary sources use either, so each dimension quoted in this record names its formulation where it matters.

Version and length of the Wang, Wang and Zhou paper. The abstract page I opened shows v2 (11 Aug 2026) and 78 pages with 6 figures. A search summary gave v1 only and '74 pages, 6 figures'. I have used the abstract page.

summary: Chern's question (first formulation: are the equators the only smooth embedded minimal hypersurfaces that are topological n-spheres in S^(n+1)?) is answered negatively in every dimension except one range, per Wikipedia's January 2024 article. That article lists the remaining unknown cases as odd ambient dimensions of 9 or more in its second formulation (even n of 8 or more in the first). I found no event touching that range. The only 2024-2026 event that bears on the sphere question itself is Wang, Wang and Zhou (arXiv 2602.03984, posted 3 Feb 2026, v2 11 Aug 2026): an embedded non-equatorial minimal S^3 in the unit S^4 by equivariant min-max. It is an unrefereed preprint. In about eight months I found no journal acceptance, referee report, expert write-up or blog post. Its own introduction lists n = 4 among Hsiang's 1983 dimensions, and Carlotto and Schulz (arXiv 2109.11768, first posted 24 Sep 2021, published Ars Inveniendi Analytica 2023) already report infinitely many embedded non-isometric hyperspheres in S^4. So the paper's 'new resolution' claim is a close call: it adds a new construction in a dimension already settled negatively, and I did not read enough to say whether it adds embeddedness or a new symmetry class. Other 2024-2026 items are recorded as discounted: Kapouleas-Zou's doubled equator in S^4 (May 2024), Carlotto-Li-Wang's persistence of Hsiang's hyperspheres under nearly round metrics (Nov 2024), Ko's cohomogeneity-two hypersurfaces with non-sphere types (Dec 2025), Chen's survey (Mar 2026), and T. Wang's embedded hypersurfaces of non-sphere types in S^4 (30 Jun 2026). The last one's Remark 1.3 says its members are either 3-spheres or S^1-bundles, and I could not resolve which. Pre-window analogues (Hsiang and Tomter's immersion paper, the Jost-Xin-Yang rigidity theorems under Gauss-image conditions, Assimos-Jost) are recorded as variants. I took the bullet's question as Chern's question, since its statement says only 'the spherical Bernstein's problem' and does not spell it out. No AI system is named in any source about this problem. The AI searches (37 queries, listed below) turned up only other 2026 AI-disclosure papers on area-minimizing hypercones and branched minimal hypersurfaces; none is about hyperspheres, and their disclosures appeared only in search snippets, not on the abstract pages I opened.
competing_reading: Reading that the 2026 Wang-Wang-Zhou paper moves the problem: it is a new min-max construction of an embedded non-equatorial hypersphere, the authors call it a new resolution, and it confirms an assertion of Pitts and Rubinstein. Read as a counterexample in S^4, it is the only 2024-2026 event that bears on Chern's question as posed. Reading against: S^4 was already settled negatively by Hsiang (1983) and, for embedded hyperspheres, by Carlotto and Schulz (2021), so the case it adds is not a new dimension. The open range Wikipedia lists is untouched, so the question's status does not change under this reading. The judging pass has to decide between these; I have not.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full Wang-Wang-Zhou text, in particular the final section, acknowledgements and references, and any passage comparing its S^4 hypersphere with Hsiang's and Carlotto-Schulz's (none of which the fetch returned), to settle what 'new' means. (2) The 1983 Hsiang papers in Annals and Inventiones, to confirm whether the S^4 examples are embedded and which dimensions Part I covers. (3) Journal status of the Wang-Wang-Zhou paper, and any written verification. (4) The Tomter 1987 Acta text, to settle the even/odd range and the convention used. (5) Any construction in an odd ambient dimension of 9 or more; none was found in the searches. (6) The full text of Wang's arXiv 2606.31091, Remark 1.3 and Section 5, to see whether any S^3 member is non-equatorial.

dead_ends: Entire minimal graphs over S^2 x R, Killing submersions, Heisenberg-group Bernstein problems: analogues, not the bullet's question; search summaries only, not recorded as events.
Chern's pinching conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces in spheres (Clifford torus rigidity, Li-Xu-Xu and others): a different problem; search snippets only.

Chern-do Carmo-Kobayashi conjecture on scalar curvature for minimal submanifolds of spheres, and the 2026 counterexample by Firester and Tsiamis (arXiv 2608.18074): a different conjecture, and the paper was not opened (search snippet only).

Other 2026 AI-disclosure claims (OpenAI GPT-5.6 and GPT-6.0, Copilot and Composer 2 on minimal hypersurfaces): the abstract pages opened for 2609.24958, 2608.27398 and 2607.29632 are not about hyperspheres and show no disclosure; the disclosures remain unverified.
DeepMind 2602.15728 (low-curvature immersion S^n x S^1, 2026): search snippet only; not about this problem.

OpenAI unit-distance (May 2026), Astra open-problems list (Aug 2026), Navier-Stokes claim (Sept 2026); AlphaEvolve kissing-number result: none concerns minimal hyperspheres per their search summaries; not opened.
Claims of Claude or another model resolving the Jacobian conjecture or the Hopf problem on S^6: different problems; news and aggregator snippets only, not verified.
Solomon (1984), cited inside the Assimos-Jost abstract as a prior rigidity result under a Gauss-image condition: not opened, not recorded as an event.
